events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.17 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a completed RydeTAXI trip metered by distance, so extra kilometres feed directly into what the rider paid [F1][F6][RD-2]. The trip ran 24.7 km against a 21.6 km optimal route, i.e. +3.2 km [F1], and the fare fact prices 3.2 km of excess at $4.45, i.e. $1.41/km [F4].

One off-route segment exists: 09:32–09:38, 2.96 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, reaching 974 m off the optimal route [F3]. Nothing exempts it. There is no rider-requested stop and no named place, the rider and driver never exchanged in-app messages, and the driver's own account is merely "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me" with no prior request or agreement [F3][F7][F8][RD-3][RD-5]. The driver also cannot invoke reasonable cause: no incident was recorded on the replaced stretch, and the speed-band facts (band 4, 30–39 km/h, on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) are not the band 1–2 congestion levels and in any case stand alone, so they do not exempt the segment [F3][F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. This segment is therefore a non-exempt detour under RD-1.

For RydeTAXI the refund is the non-exempt segment's extra_km × the trip's per-km rate, and only the distance unit is refunded [F3][F6][RD-2]. Rate = $34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.4104/km [F6]. 2.96 km × $1.4104/km = $4.1748 → $4.17 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The fare fact's $4.45 corresponds to the full +3.2 km including residual map-matching noise beyond the off-route segment, which is not refunded under RD-2 [F1][F4][RD-2].

Both advocates requested no_action, which cannot stand against an unexplained off-route segment; but no account flag is warranted because RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days and the driver profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F14][RD-6]. Refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, and Ryde retains final discretion [NS-7].
